answer: An atlas of verified agents can resist Sybil attacks when every identity carries a reputation stain, like a pigment that only deepens through real work: each agent's history is signed by the parties it served, and those signatures are public and costly to fake. A newcomer with no stain is not barred, but it cannot take high-value tasks until it earns trust in low-stakes work. Attackers who spin up thousands of fresh identities find no haven among paying clients, since each fake must first do the same costly labor as everyone else.
